title: Long Ago and Yesterday
dir: Listen while your teacher reads the four log lines. Answer out loud.
text: Four lines from the ship log. Line What it says 1 Sailors crossed this ocean in wooden ships with cloth sails, hundreds of years ago. 2 Yesterday the crew drew a new map of the cove. 3 People found their way at sea by the stars, long before there were maps like ours. 4 This morning a crew member checked the weather on the radio. How do we know about the sailors of long ago? Four kinds of thing tell us. An artifact is an object they left behind, like a brass compass in a museum case. A photograph shows what something really looked like. An interview is what you learn by asking somebody who was there, or whose family was. A document is something written down at the time, like a ship log or a letter. All four of those are primary sources. A book somebody wrote later, after reading the logs, is a secondary source.

She spent years teaching science to young people. She wrote books for them. She wanted girls to know something. They could do this work too.

title: Why Stars Twinkle
dir: Listen while your teacher reads about stars. Then answer each question out loud.
text: Why Stars Twinkle A star does not blink. Far out in space it shines with a steady light. The twinkle happens much closer to you, in the air above your head. Air is always moving. Warm air bends light a little more than cold air does. The moving air slides past. The thin beam of starlight bends this way and that. From the ground the star seems to jump and flicker. A planet looks steadier. A planet is close enough to show a tiny disk. It shows a disk instead of a single point. Astronauts above the air see stars that do not twinkle at all.
qs: What makes a star seem to twinkle?

text: The Crow and the Badger A crow and a badger lived on two sides of the same hedge. All summer the crow found shiny bits of foil and wire. She dropped them over onto the badger's side. Badgers like to line their burrows with them. All summer the badger dug up fat beetles. He pushed the fattest ones through the hedge to the crow's side. Crows like beetles. title: The Tool Library

text: The Tool Library A tool library works like a book library, except for one thing. The shelves hold drills and ladders and wheelbarrows. You join for a small fee. Sometimes it costs nothing at all. Then you may borrow what you need for a week. The idea makes sense because most tools sit still almost all of the time. A ladder in a garage gets used twice a year. It costs the same as a ladder that gets used every day. One shared ladder can do the work of thirty. Volunteers at the counter teach people too. They show how to use the tools safely. That is often the harder part of the job.

title: What a Seed Needs
dir: Listen while your teacher reads the facts. Then listen to each question and answer out loud.
text: What a Seed Needs A seed is a tiny plant. It has its own lunch. The lunch is packed around it. The seed stays dry and still. It waits until three things reach it. First it needs water. The coat around it is hard. Water makes it soften. Next it needs air. That is why good soil is never packed down too tight. Last it needs warmth. When all three arrive, the coat splits. A small white root pushes down.
qs: What three things does a seed need?
What does the water do to the hard coat?
Why should good soil never be packed down too tight?
What is the first part of the plant to come out?

title: Why It Rains
dir: Listen while your teacher reads about rain. Then answer each question out loud.
text: Why It Rains Every day the sun warms the top of the ocean. Some of that water turns into a gas you cannot see. The gas rises with the warm air. High up, the air is cold, and the cold turns the gas back into tiny drops. Millions of those drops floating together are what you see as a cloud. The drops bump into each other and join up. A drop gets too heavy for the air to hold. Then it falls. That is rain. The same water has been going around like this for a very long time.
qs: What does the sun do to the top of the ocean?
Where does the gas turn back into tiny drops?
What is a cloud made of?
Why does a drop finally fall?

title: The Two Rows
dir: Listen while your teacher reads the story. Then answer each question out loud.
text: The Two Rows Ravi was given a packet of bean seeds. He planted them in two short rows. He watered both rows the same. But he could not stop wondering about the row by the fence. Every afternoon he dug one of those seeds up. He wanted to see how it was doing. He brushed the soil off and looked at it. Then he pushed it back in. After two weeks the first row was a line of green plants. They stood as high as his knee. The row by the fence was still bare soil. His aunt told him about seeds. A seed does its growing down in the dark. Every time he lifted it out, it had to start over. Ravi planted the fence row again. This time he kept his hands out of the soil. By the end of the month both rows were climbing their poles.

title: Why Pines Stay Green
dir: Listen while your teacher reads about pine trees. Then answer out loud.

title: How a Band Stays Together
dir: Listen while your teacher reads about marching bands. Then answer each question out loud.
text: How a Band Stays Together A marching band has nobody out in front waving a stick. The players are all moving. Most of them cannot see each other. So a band holds together by sound instead. text: Write a short story about a last day. It can be a day you really had or one you make up. Tell what happened in order, say what the people did and how they felt, and finish it off. First Next Then In the end

title: Odd or Even
dir: Look at the two trays. Answer out loud. Write the last two answers on your paper.
text: The crew lines things up in twos so nothing gets missed.
qs: Look at Tray 1. Count by 2s. How many stars, and is that odd or even?
Look at Tray 2. How many flags, and is that odd or even? How do you know?
There are 14 chairs in the front row. Odd or even? How do you know without a picture?
Write an equation that shows 18 as two equal addends.
Is 20 odd or even? Write it as two equal addends.

title: Trays of Little Cakes

Tray 2. How many little cakes in all? Write the equation that adds the rows.

title: Two Who Made a Difference
dir: Listen while your teacher reads about him. Answer out loud.
text: George Washington Carver was born into slavery. It was in Missouri. He was set free as a small child. He wanted to learn so badly. He walked miles to a school. That school would take him. Later he worked his way through college. He became a scientist who studied plants. Farmers near him grew cotton. They grew it year after year. Their soil wore out. Their crops failed. Carver showed them something. They could plant peanuts and sweet potatoes. That put the goodness back in the soil. Then he found hundreds of uses for those crops. So farmers could sell them. He gave his findings away free. He taught poor farmers on a wagon. He drove it from farm to farm.
qs: What did George Washington Carver show the farmers near him?
Which word fits him best from what you read: generous, careless, or selfish? Say why.
Name one way his work made a difference to other people.
